newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cemig surges on selloff rumors.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cemig surges on selloff rumors.

text.p: Common shares of Brazilian power firm Cemig surged more than 10 percent by late afternoon on rumors about Minas Gerais state's plan to sell a third of company voting stock, an analyst said.
Common shares of state-owned Cemig were up 4.20 reais at 44.00 reais by 1645 local/1445 EDT on the Sao Paulo bourse.

One stock market analyst said the shares priced jumped on a rumor Minas Gerais officials had struck a deal with a Chilean firm, but added the talk may stem from news the Minas Governor Eduardo Azeredo is on an official visit to Santiago.
"We heard a rumor they were going to sell to a Chilean firm and that it was a good price" one broker said.

Another dealer said all Brazilian power shares were higher on optimism about the sector's ongoing privatization but Cemig was the top gainer. "It must be that they're farther along in the privatization process," he explained.

The state plans to sell a 33 percent stake in Cemig at a December auction. Four foreign firms have expressed interest in bidding on the shares, but it is not known which will make the best offer, a company official said.
"We'll only know on the day of the auction," he said, adding U.S.-based Southern Electric, France's EDF, Canada's Hydro Quebec and Chile's Chilectra all have expressed interest.
We know that among his planned activities, the governor plans to make a visit to Chilectra, but that's all we know," the official added.
The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange was off 0.26 percent overall at 66,139 points 45 minutes before the close, with Cemig preferred up 0.90 reais or 2.74 percent at 33.80 reais.
